Write one file per item into /Users/shaun/Code/DEVELOPMENT/gate-a-sealed/run-2/out/, named <id>.json, plus your output file that the Return part of this brief names. You write in no Git repo and need no worktree.
Context: The form is one request of a skill search. Its format:
{ "id": "<the item id from tasks.json>",
  "facts": { "writes_code": true or false, "languages": ["<language term>", ...] },
  "activity": "<one activity term>",
  "touches": ["<touches term>", ...],
  "must_have": ["<quality term>", ...],
  "artefacts": ["<artefact term>", ...],
  "needs": ["<free text>", ...],
  "evidence": [ { "term": "<a term you set>", "quote": "<words copied exactly from the item's outcome, evidence or owns text>" } ] }
Rules of the form: every field except needs and evidence takes only terms of terms.json, from the group whose request field it is; activity is one term and the other term fields are lists, which may be empty. Set a term only when the task text supports it, and give each term of activity, touches, must_have and artefacts one evidence entry whose quote is copied word for word from that item's outcome, evidence or owns text; a fact may have one too. facts.writes_code says whether the task writes or changes source code; facts.languages lists the programming languages of the code it writes or changes, as vocabulary terms. Leave out repo_has and repo_dependencies: code fills them from the repo later. needs holds at most three short free-text needs, each one a thing the task needs help with that the terms do not say, written in your own short words; leave it empty when the terms say it all. Use aliases.json to map a word of the task to its term. An item with row "role" is a role (for example a reviewer) with no task of its own: fill its form for the work that role does. The assembled brief may carry a charter line that names a specification file; it is background only: do not open it, because it holds the answers this test measures.
Acceptance: /Users/shaun/Code/DEVELOPMENT/gate-a-sealed/run-2/out/ holds 23 files, one per item of tasks.json, each a JSON object in the format above. Your output file lists the files you wrote and, for each item where you were unsure of a term, the item id, the field and why; it also lists every file you read, which must be the three input files only.
